findings.evidence: PhaseSpace.lean:412-425 (`hrot` has no `m` on the right-hand side; `L` is a local `let`). Physlib Relativity/LorentzGroup/Rotations.lean:78 defines `ofSpecialOrthogonal.invFun Λ := ⟨fun i j => Λ.1.1 (Sum.inr i) (Sum.inr j), _⟩`, exactly the block `hrot` sums over, with membership in `Matrix.specialOrthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ` already proved there.
findings.fix: Expose the general statement and derive the rest from it: add `massShellAction_rotation_apply (Λ : Rotations d) (m : ℝ) (p) (j) : massShellAction Λ m p j = ∑ k, (Λ : LorentzGroup d).1 (Sum.inr j) (Sum.inr k) * p k` (one line from `spatialPart_rotations_smul_apply` + `spatialPart_massShell`), hence mass-independence, and get `norm_massShellAction_rotation` and Lebesgue-measure preservation from it. Equivalently, strengthen `spatialPart_rotations_smul_apply` in RotationsExtensions.lean to the matrix form `((Λ : LorentzGroup d) • v).spatialPart = (ofSpecialOrthogonal.symm Λ).1.mulVec v.spatialPart`, so the isometry comes from `Matrix.mem_specialOrthogonalGroup_iff` rather than being rebuilt by hand.
findings.issue: `hrot` (line 412-414) proves `massShellAction Λ m p j = ∑ k, Λ.1 (Sum.inr j) (Sum.inr k) * p k`, i.e. the rotation action on momenta does not depend on `m` at all, and `let L` (415-423) builds the corresponding linear isometry; both stay private to the proof. The public rotation API (`onShellEnergy_massShellAction_rotation` 395, `norm_massShellAction_rotation` 401, `massShell_massShellAction_rotation` 387) is all mass-indexed, and `norm_massShellAction_rotation` is derived by squaring the energy identity instead of from the isometry that the proof already has.

summary: Hypotheses and the `Λ`-generality of the main definitions are at the right level, but the rotation section proves the general fact inline and exposes only mass-indexed specializations: for `Λ : Rotations d` the action on spatial momenta is independent of `m` and is a linear isometry, yet that object is built inside `measurePreserving_massShellAction_rotation` and never stated.
